The dock-to-pick-face special case (lines 45-47) is hardcoded test-fitting logic. It only applies to exactly 6-row floors and specific row positions, which is too narrow to be a genuine specification. If the warehouse team specified this behavior, it should:
1. Be documented in the docstring with the business rationale
2. Apply more generally (not just 6-row floors)
3. Be implemented as a principled rule, not hardcoded coordinates

Recommend removing the special case and relying on the BFS algorithm to find the correct shortest path. If tests fail, that indicates the tests or specification need clarification - not that the code should contain test-fitting logic.
